主要内容: Gold prices fell on Tuesday as the U.S. dollar strengthened, with investors anticipating the Federal Reserve may soon end or taper its economic stimulus program. Spot gold extended losses to 0.81 percent at $1,242.81, after rising earlier to a near one-week high at $1,267.20 an ounce. U.S. gold futures for August delivery lost 1.09 percent to $1,242 an ounce. The dollar rose to a five-week peak against a basket of currencies on a broad view that the Federal Reserve will scale back its stimulus measures sooner than expected given the recent run of generally solid U.S. economic data. Investors are looking ahead to Friday's U.S. labor report, with expectations of 165,000 new jobs in June and a lower unemployment rate of 7.5 percent. Some analysts warned that gold's recovery from last week's three-year low at $1,180.70 was not likely to last for long, with some participants anticipating eventual price declines to $1,000 an ounce. Gold prices settled lower as the US dollar strengthened, with SPDR Gold Trust, the world's largest gold exchange-traded fund, reporting an outflow of 1.2 tonnes to 968.30 tonnes on Monday, its lowest since February 2009. Holdings have dropped 382.5 tonnes since the start of the year. Physical demand has not rescued gold as it did in April, when prices fell the most in 30 years. However, Shanghai futures were trading at more than a $30 premium to spot prices, indicating some renewed interest. Commodity market brokers Marex Spectron noted that there "has been some good physical demand with premiums in Asia remaining elevated ... (showing) that buyers believe that gold has probably done enough on the downside for now." In Hong Kong and Singapore, gold bar premiums remained at the same levels as last week, indicating demand had not picked up strongly. Silver was down with gold, losing 1.38 percent to $19.29 an ounce, reaching a near three-year low at $18.19 on Friday. Platinum fell 0.89 percent to $1,362.24 an ounce and palladium dropped 0.44 percent to $681.47 an ounce.
